name: Reference-Class and Evidence Update

positioning.oneLineSummary: Uses an explicitly selected reference-class distribution as a prior and updates it only with evidence whose relevance and likelihood are stated.
positioning.productLabel: Base-Rate Update Lens — based on Mauboussin-affiliated public research
notAClaimOf: base rates determining an individual outcome
a convenient industry average being a valid reference class
Bayesian language making unsupported probabilities precise

attribution.display: Based on Michael J. Mauboussin and Dan Callahan's public Bayes and Base Rates research

neutralParaphrase: Choose a reference class that matches the company and question on stage, business model, geography, cohort, and measurement. Treat its full distribution as a prior, document selection and survivorship limits, then update with company-specific evidence. If likelihoods cannot be defensibly quantified, preserve the update as directional rather than manufacturing a posterior.

locator.value: Public report: reference-class selection, prior distributions, evidence updating, and changing base-rate distributions
Chapter 7: expected value, margin of safety, and base rates

requiredConditions: The forecast question and outcome measure are precisely defined.
Reference-class inclusion, exclusion, cohort, stage, geography, and measurement are recorded.
The full distribution and missing-data biases are available.
Company-specific update evidence is distinct from evidence used to choose the class.

requiredEvidence.description: Versioned dataset and rules for a relevant cohort, including outcome distribution and censoring.
Evidence supporting similarity on stage, business model, geography, capital intensity, cohort, and metric definition.
Company-specific evidence and, if numeric Bayes is used, validated likelihood ratios or conditional distributions.

decisionQuestions: What exact outcome is being forecast?
Which reference class is closest and why?
How were failures, censored outcomes, and changing cohorts handled?
What company-specific evidence should update the prior?
Are numeric likelihoods validated or only directional?
What alternative reference class would change the conclusion?
positiveSignals: The reference class is defined before viewing the desired outcome.
The cohort matches stage, model, geography, and measurement.
Failures and censored cases are retained.
Company-specific evidence has validated predictive relevance.
redFlags: The class is chosen because its average supports the thesis.
Only successful companies appear in the dataset.
A mean replaces the outcome distribution.
Company storytelling overrides the prior without update evidence.
Unsupported likelihood ratios create false posterior precision.
disconfirmingEvidence: A closer reference class has materially different outcomes.
The dataset excludes failures, shutdowns, or down rounds.
Metric definitions differ from the company evidence.
The cohort is structurally obsolete after technology or regulation change.
Alleged company-specific signals have weak out-of-sample predictive value.
contraindications: Do not use a reference class without documented selection rules.
Do not convert directional evidence into numeric Bayes without validated likelihoods.
Do not treat the prior as an individual-company verdict.
Do not let the LLM calculate a posterior.

instructions: Define the outcome and select the reference class before evaluating the desired answer.
Audit class fit, distribution, censoring, and temporal relevance.
Separate class-selection evidence from company-update evidence.
Run a deterministic update only when validated likelihood inputs exist; otherwise state a directional update.
Report alternative classes, counterevidence, and posterior uncertainty.

sourceReliability.low: The base rate comes from anecdotes or an opaque database.
sourceReliability.medium: The dataset is credible but class fit or censoring is incomplete.
sourceReliability.high: The dataset, cohort rules, failures, metrics, and updates are auditable.

evidenceStrength.medium: A relevant prior and directional update exist.
evidenceStrength.high: A matched prior and validated update model support a bounded posterior.

evidenceCoverage.medium: Distribution and company evidence exist but cohort drift or censoring remains.
evidenceCoverage.high: Distribution, class fit, failures, drift, update evidence, and alternatives are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.medium: A class exists but the company is an edge case.
applicabilityConfidence.high: The question and company match a well-defined cohort.

judgmentConfidence.low: Only class-selection uncertainty can be reported.
judgmentConfidence.medium: A prior and directional update are defensible.
judgmentConfidence.high: A reproducible update with sensitivity is supportable.

promotionRequirements: Approve reference-class governance and dataset versions.
Validate likelihood models out of sample.
Audit cohort drift and survivorship controls.
empiricalQualifications: Reference classes involve judgment and can be manipulated.
Startup cohorts evolve rapidly and historical distributions may drift.
Company evidence is often dependent, making naive sequential updates misleading.

rights.notes: This card primarily reflects later Mauboussin-affiliated public research, not a joint Rappaport attribution.

openIssues: Define supported reference-class datasets and drift policy.
